The two PLO edges (PLO 1437, PLO 2121) revoke in part power-site 'EO of May 27, 1913' land orders of the same date, not this designation (doctrine sec. (c) says the same).

jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_1932.txt (and numbered-early-orders slice EO_1932__CSR_1914_i133.txt, same words), May 6, 1914: 'The Secretary of Agriculture recommends the promotion of Mr. Augusterfer, who has been in the department since April, 1904'. The named person was alive in April 1904, i.e. on or before 1904-04-30 (Appendix A rule: month without a day = last day of the month), which is before 1904-05-03. Latest possible death 1904-04-30 + 122 y 164 d = 2026-10-11, before the cutoff. This is exactly the B13 dated-presence fact; the B99 basis 'no dated presence before 1904' is false for this member. One named person only.
correct_lead: no, TERM (life of named person, dated presence; hand_checked_dated_fact), interval (1914-05-06, 2026-10-11]; quote 'has been in the department since April, 1904'

evidence: jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6218-appointment-david-gates.txt (and hathi-gpo-orders EO_6218.txt, same words), July 26, 1933: 'Mr. David A. Gates may be appointed as an Internal Revenue Agent ... without regard to the requirements of the civil-service rules for a period of one year from the date of this order' and 'The particular position ... is withdrawn from the provisions of the civil-service rules during the period of his incumbency.' The order fixes its own term from the order date, so on either reading (one-year window or one-year appointment) its command ended no later than 1934-07-26. This is the same own-terms pattern the doctrine decides in B08b/B08c (EO 4452, EO 3940). The age route is correctly unavailable ('Chief of Revenue Agents during the years 1906 to 1908' is after 1904), but the lead ignores the stated term.
correct_lead: no, TERM (term_expired), fixed 1934-07-26 (one year from the order date of 1933-07-26)

jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_4505.txt, September 9, 1926 (member record carries only the year 1926): 'Mrs. Edith P. Schaffer, an employee in the General Accounting Office, is hereby restored to her former classified status.' The order does not permit a later action; it takes the one action itself on issue. Under the doctrine's own M1 ('Its command is used up when the action is taken') and its persistence note (acquired status survives as a consequence, not as the order's command), the command was exhausted on 1926-09-09. The B99 basis ('The permission ended when used ... but neither date is shown') is false for this member: the use date is the order date. The doctrine has no branch for self-executing one-person acts, so the owner may need to confirm the reading, but the held text decides it.
